content:
maria: Seeing a big spike in retries and uneven traffic distribution to our model-serving service in eu-west-1 GPU pool. Pod metrics show one endpoint getting ~75-80% of connections and the rest barely any.  

ajay: ugh, that sounds like an IPVS hash/endpoint skew. Any recent kube-proxy or kernel changes rolled?

maria: kube-proxy was rotated yesterday to 1.29.3 -> 1.30.0 on the gpu node pools as part of a small control-plane bump. Noticed this right after. 

liam: can you paste ipvs stats and service config? quick checks: `kubectl -n kube-system exec -c kube-proxy <kube-proxy-pod> -- ipvsadm -Ln --stats` and `kubectl get ep -o wide`

maria: paste logs + outputs: 
```
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP 10.3.45.12:8500 rr
  -> 10.3.67.11:8500             Route    1      142       0
  -> 10.3.67.12:8500             Route    1       12       0
  -> 10.3.67.13:8500             Route    1       10       0
  -> 10.3.67.14:8500             Route    1       15       0
  -> 10.3.67.15:8500             Route    1      800       0
```

maria: the last endpoint (10.3.67.15) is one of the GPU nodes; it holds ~800 active conns while others are single digits. 

nora: that looks like a connection-hotspot not weight-based. Could be RSS hashing on the NIC combined with IPVS destination hash causing RSS to send most flows to one queue, and one CPU handling them -> backlog. Also check if MTU mismatch exists on the path (we have mixed jumbo/standard config in that rack).

ajay: good point. RDMA/VPP/OVS or NIC offloads could cause skew. Run these: `ethtool -k eth0` on node, `cat /proc/net/ip_vs_stats`, and `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing`. Also `ss -tn sport = :8500` to inspect client IP distribution.

maria: ran `ethtool -k` on the hotspot node: 
```
Generic offload parameters for eth0:
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
udp-fragmentation-offload: on
lro: off
rx-vlan-offload: on
```
mtu on that node is 9000. other nodes MTU=1500.

liam: MTU mismatch incoming -> fragmentation or black-holing for larger frames. RoCE RDMA expects consistent MTU; when it's mixed, packets take weird paths and can cause retransmits at TCP level. That could make one node appear to be handling more flows because smaller frames succeed to one NIC and others drop or stall.

nora: can we confirm with tcpdump? run `tcpdump -i eth0 -nn -s 1200 'port 8500'` on both a healthy node and hotspot node and compare retransmits/dup acks.

maria: ran quick capture: hotspot node shows a lot of `TCP Retransmission` and `PSH, ACK` bursts; healthy node shows mostly `ACK` steady. 

ajay: what about ipvs scheduler? it's `rr` in the output but IPVS rr is flow-hash-based for TCP and depends on conntrack. There was a known edge case where `--hashmode` or kernel hash seed interacts badly with RSS resulting in skew. We can try switching scheduler to `sh` (source hashing) temporarily and see distribution. `kubectl -n kube-system edit configmap kube-proxy` -> set `mode: ipvs` and `ipvs: scheduler: sh` or pass `--ipvs-scheduler=sh` to kube-proxy DaemonSet.

liam: or toggle `--iptables` mode for a quick test to see if iptables evens out distribution. iptables will NAT and may have different balancing behavior (but increases CPU).

nora: remediation plan: (1) schedule a small probe change during low-traffic: change kube-proxy scheduler to `sh` for gpu pool nodes, (2) standardize MTU to 1500 across the rack (coord with infra-net), (3) disable risky offloads temporarily (`ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`) on that NIC to test, (4) monitor conn distribution + packet loss.

maria: I'm on (1) now. applying patch to kube-proxy DaemonSet on a single node via nodeSelector to limit impact. will post results.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-987 - ipvs endpoint skew eu-west-1 GPU pool. Assigned to eng-infra.

ajay: if (1) fixes distribution we can roll; if not, revert and try iptables mode. Also open a ticket with NIC vendor for RSS hash behavior.

maria: update 10m later: changed scheduler to `sh` on the probe node -> connections now roughly even (80/90 per endpoint). Retransmits dropped substantially. 

liam: nice! That indicates hashing mismatch with rr+RSS. Next steps: schedule MTU normalization across that rack and roll the kube-proxy change cluster-wide after coordination. Also add an e2e test to our upgrade playbook that validates endpoint distribution (simple curl load test + ipvsadm check) after kube-proxy upgrades.

nora: agree. I'll create a runbook entry: checks to run after kube-proxy upgrades: ipvsadm stats, ethtool offload list, MTU sanity, capture sample tcpdump.

maria: tagging @networking to standardize MTU on the eu-west-1-gpu rack. For immediate mitigation rolling kube-proxy scheduler to `sh` for GPU node pools. :thumbsup: 

ajay: also adding `tcp_mtu_probing=1` on affected nodes as a precaution and documenting why (less likely to black-hole). Run: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`

maria: thanks everyone. I'll keep monitoring and close the incident once all GPU nodes are normalized and distribution stays balanced for 24h. :white_check_mark:
